steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I'm back.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: No problems, I take it?

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Nothing of particular note within a thirty kilometer range. The area is safe for now.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Very good. Let me take a look at the map.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: We're on the right track. Keep north, and we should see a waypoint the locals called Trumhill before long.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: We'll have an opportunity to rest at its base. From there, we can start moving west, and we'll be at Phecon within two days.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Is Phecon our destination?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Of course not, but it's the most suitable transfer station. Phecon sees a lot of Columbian caravans, which we can follow one to reach Twinriver. There, we have a Rhodes Island branch office.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: If we can get to the branch office, we'll be able to secure ourselves some transportation. From there, the rest will be much easier.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Music to my ears! Can't wait to wrap up this on-foot odyssey. My shoe soles are worn straight flat.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: You ought to walk outside more. It's good for your health, and you won't need to keep worrying so much about your weight.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Hey!

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: What about the communicator? Any linkable signal nodes?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Still no good. The way I see it, we're not going to get any direct contact with the Rhodes Island landship until we reach Phecon.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Not unless we can get our hands on a more powerful transmitter...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You can forget about that. There's no other nomadic city to be found around here.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Quite. That's why I made sure to ask you to bring more than enough food and water. It's a tall order to find any supplies on the way to Phecon.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I do remember little settlements dotted around here and there, but after all these years, I could hardly say whether any of them are still where they used to be.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: So you're pretty familiar with this area, Mr. Rangers.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hah-hah-hah... I might've been a tad more familiar in my sprightlier days. Truth is, I haven't been around these wastelands in a long, long time.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: You drew that map yourself, Mr. Rangers?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Indeed. Any good ranger can draw their own maps, though I never would've guessed this one would still be useful even now. The topography around here hasn't been marred by Catastrophes too badly, so we might count ourselves lucky.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I'm sorry for all the bother we've made for you.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Don't you worry about it. It's this old man's duty to look out for you young'uns.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I share the responsibility for this mess, anyway. We wouldn't be in such a tight spot now if I had made the proper preparations beforehand.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: What, the band of mysterious mercenaries that raided the warehouse and by rotten luck just happened to make off with our car?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Who's going to believe a story like that? ?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: I think it was the trader, actually. Pulled our car apart to sell off the parts, then fed us some random explanation to cover up after the fact.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I actually agree with you, for once.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You didn't need the 'for once'.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: The old me wouldn't have let him off as kindly as that, if we were going by our old Blacksteel mercenary customs.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: But you are Rhodes Island operators now. I'd much rather not see you get into fights with the locals.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: The medical supplies made it safely, and the trader didn't try to cook the books when paying us. We can't really ask for too much more.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: Carrying a sack of refined Originium Ingots across the barrenlands by foot is incredibly dangerous.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I won't deny how... perforated their explanations were. We can't count on the local Vouivre mercenaries to be totally honest with us, so I'll keep an eye out for that next time.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: But in the meantime, once we get back, you do have to report the property loss to Logistics.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: *Sigh*... Yeah, this is just how Vouivre is.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That said...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I could likely find our way there even without any maps or Arts, but we'd be taking time we don't have. I worry we're too many for that, and our water and food wouldn't last us.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: You can navigate the Sargon barrens without any tools? May I ask how?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: If we ever have the time in future, I can teach you a thing or two. It's all nothing more than my experience.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: How do I put it...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: You're very worthy of the 'Ranger of the Red Valley' title, if I do say so.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hah-hah-hah-hah. So you youngsters know how to tell an old tale or two as well, then.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That's just an exaggerated title.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Aren't those tales all true, though? Like how you rounded up and brought all of the Jenkins Seven to justice in a single day, or how you held off an entire column of Rusthammer Bandits all by yourself...

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: How you struck ten targets with just a single arrow, or how you shot down a Lateranan's bullets while high up in the sky...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: My word. So this is what the stories are like now.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: My Sargon colleagues at Blacksteel spoke of your tales from time to time, Mr. Rangers. They're all like this, pretty much. Stories not out of place in a theater.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: They wouldn't be out of place in a novel either.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: You've heard them too, right, Miss Schwarz?

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: There was a mercenary traveling the breadth of Columbia who told me about one or two of them.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: I believe they were 'The Scimitar of the Bloody Valley' and 'Tragedy of the Lord Ameer'.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Mm... A little exaggerated indeed.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Rangers aren't as all-powerful as they've been portrayed.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: I can't suppose to know what you've all heard, but I can say that the most widespread stories are largely untrue.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Rangers were not a fighting force. If you want my description, they were more akin to survivors banded together out in the wild.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: They started as just a couple of ordinary folk fallen into times of pain and strife. They stepped forth against the odds, against it all. They protected villages against the scourges that would pillage them.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: They weren't trained warriors, any of them. They were a resistance, born in a time of war that knew no other way, of devastation that took and took and took.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: They brimmed with anger under it. They refused to keel to cruel destiny through the months and years of the war.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Afterwards, as more and more joined them, they slowly grew from a lone autonomous militia of sorts to a collective of regional organizations, and so they resided across the wastelands, defending settlements while offering medical aid.

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: I've read of that from my time at Blacksteel. From reports of the Sargon region, it wasn't just officials, but the rangers as well who'd pursue wasteland hooligans and mercenary looters to exhaustion, out across the wastelands.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: What those reports refer to is truth, I can say that.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Back then, a group of rangers certainly... had its heroes, and they certainly caught themselves a fair share of villains. The events you describe happened, but I stress that that wasn't standard fare.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: The vast majority of the time, we rangers simply helped towns fix their wells, fend off wild beasts, gather medicine, that kind of stuff. Just the little things.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Moreover, this area wasn't even Sargon territory back then...

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: So, Mr. Rangers, back then, you must've been part of that group of 'heroes,' right?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hah-hah-hah. This old man is hardly so prestigious. I was but a normal scout and nothing more.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: ...Normal...?

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: In the end, this organization of rangers ended up disbanding, didn't it?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: That certainly is a long story...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Many things happened afterwards, to say the least. And once the war concluded, the Lord Ameers were settled, each with all the land they wanted.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Those Lord Ameers of Sargon would not tolerate an organization that bowed to no-one, and the rangers were one such organization.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Of course, opinion from the Lord Ameers aside, there were many reasons why the rangers disbanded. But these are past events, and it's been a very, very long time since. The nitty-gritty of it all has fallen out of this old man's head.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: So all those wild stories never actually happened?

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: The truth is often mundane. So you remedy it by exaggerating how things happened, and you make the story dramatic.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: And only when it's dramatic enough do people pass it down.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Your stories all picked up layers upon layers of artistry before they reached you.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Alright, this old man's told plenty enough himself. Let's get ourselves ready to leave.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: By the sound of things, we've already reached Sargon territory?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: We were already in Sargon as of last night. Can you please pay a little attention? When suddenly you're in trouble, I'll be the last one to help you.

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: I love how much you suck.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: The land we step on now is the jurisdiction of the Lord Ameer of Bayalir, though his provisional capital is still a ways away.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: After that...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Hold! Stop moving!

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: ...You heard that too.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: All of you, stay still. Something's approaching.

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: ...It's close...

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: It's underneath us! Scatter!

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Franka! Move!

steps.name: Hideous Monstrosity
steps.text: (Roars)

steps.name: Schwarz
steps.text: What... what are these?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: Are these... sand beasts?

steps.name: Franka
steps.text: Since when do sand beasts grow like this?

steps.name: Liskarm
steps.text: One, two... no, there's just too many.

steps.name: Rangers
steps.text: Move into formation! Be ready for battle!
